title: Four ways to leave a VPC privately
claim: A peering connection joins two VPCs, a transit gateway joins many, and endpoints reach one service privately.
alt: VPC A and VPC B joined by one peering connection. Three spoke VPCs attached to a transit gateway. A spoke VPC with a gateway endpoint to Amazon S3 and an interface endpoint to a service in a provider VPC.

edges.label: Peering
edges.say: VPC A and VPC B talk over one peering connection, as if they are within the same network.
Each spoke VPC only needs to connect to the transit gateway to reach the other attached VPCs.
A gateway endpoint will add an entry to your route table you selected for Amazon S3.
An interface endpoint reaches one endpoint service, and it is a one-way service.

notes: Brief 11 hero (1-fast.md#in-one-breath). Title, claim, alt equal 1-fast.md. Step 1 follows 1-fast.md (verbatim display of vpc-peering-def-private-ipv4-ipv6); steps 2 to 4 equal brief.json. Two columns fit a phone: peering is a direct edge between two VPCs, the transit gateway is a hub of three spokes, the third spoke owns the endpoints.
